behavior_items: The reproducer targets a variadic-call ABI mismatch involving an empty aggregate type named something like `Dummy` and a function that reads later arguments through `va_list`.

Its core setup is a call to a variadic function where one of the variable arguments is an instance of an empty struct/class, followed by additional scalar arguments; the function then consumes the arguments with `va_arg` under the assumption that each passed argument advances the variable-argument cursor according to the platform ABI.

In C++, an empty class/struct is a valid complete object type and has nonzero size, so passing such an object as a by-value variadic argument participates in argument passing and consumes ABI space/register classification as an actual argument.

In C, truly empty structs are a GNU extension rather than standard C, and GCC historically treated them differently from C++ during lowering and ABI classification; the bug report explicitly states that the same source shape is passed differently in C and C++.

Because the variadic callee does not have type information for the `...` arguments, correct execution depends entirely on caller and callee agreeing on the exact ABI layout of every unnamed argument, including unusual aggregate types such as an empty struct.

The failure mode reported is that the function prints garbage for the sixth argument, which indicates that after the empty-struct argument, `va_list` traversal becomes misaligned with the actual call frame/register save area.

That symptom means the empty struct is effectively counted as consuming argument position/space on one side of the call boundary but not on the other side, or is classified with a different size/alignment rule, so every subsequent `va_arg` reads the wrong location.

The reproducer is sensitive specifically to the empty/non-empty distinction: adding any member to the struct makes the output correct because a non-empty aggregate has an unambiguous ABI size and calling convention, restoring agreement between call expansion and `va_arg` walking.

This exercises GCC front-end and ABI-lowering behavior rather than libc logic: `va_list` machinery in the library follows the target ABI, but if GCC emits different conventions for the same source-level variadic argument depending on language mode, the library-level access sequence will appear corrupted.

On x86-64 System V, where variadic handling tracks register and stack slots with strict size/class rules, such a disagreement readily causes later integer arguments to be fetched from the wrong general-register save slot or stack address, matching the observed garbage output.

The bug report therefore points to inconsistent handling of empty aggregate by-value arguments between the C and C++ front ends when passed through `...`, causing ABI incompatibility and downstream `va_list` corruption.

The reproducer does not require undefined behavior from reading an argument with the wrong requested type; instead, it relies on a caller/callee disagreement introduced by the compiler itself for an edge-case type, making it a compiler code-generation/ABI conformance bug.

The practical lesson exercised by the test is that variadic interfaces are extremely fragile around nonstandard or language-specific aggregate types, and empty structs/classes are especially problematic because C and C++ assign them different semantic status and historically GCC mapped that difference into incompatible call layouts.
test_behavior_analysis.summary: The reproducer demonstrates a GCC ABI/code-generation bug for variadic calls involving an empty struct/class passed by value. In C++ the empty type is treated as a real object argument, while in GNU C GCC historically handled the empty struct differently, so caller-side argument layout and callee-side `va_list` traversal disagree. As a result, every argument after the empty struct is read from the wrong location, producing garbage output for the later argument. Adding a member to the struct removes the ambiguity because the aggregate then has a normal, consistent ABI representation.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The common pattern is an ABI disagreement for variadic arguments after a by-value empty aggregate. The reproducer places an empty struct/class in the unnamed argument list, then reads later scalar arguments with `va_arg`. The reported corruption of a later argument shows that caller-side argument layout and callee-side `va_list` traversal no longer agree once the empty aggregate is encountered. The critical clue is that behavior differs between C and C++ and disappears when the struct is made non-empty. That strongly indicates a GCC language-dependent lowering/classification bug for empty aggregates in variadic calls, not a problem in the reproducer. In practice, this points to compiler code that decides whether an empty aggregate consumes size, alignment, register slots, or stack slots for `...` arguments, or code that builds the `va_arg` view of such arguments, being inconsistent across front ends or target ABI hooks.
possible_causes: Incorrect target ABI classification of empty struct/class arguments passed through `...`, causing GCC to treat the argument as zero-sized in GNU C but as a real object in C++.

Mismatch between caller-side call expansion and callee-side variadic access logic for empty aggregates, so the caller omits or compresses the empty argument while `va_list` advancement assumes it consumed a slot, or vice versa.

Front-end dependent type layout/size handling for empty records leaking into ABI lowering, with C and C++ producing different `TYPE_SIZE`/mode semantics for the same empty aggregate during argument passing.
Bug in the x86-64 System V argument passing hook for BLKmode/aggregate values where zero-sized or empty records are not assigned register or stack consumption consistently for variadic calls.

Incorrect implementation of default argument promotion / unnamed-argument lowering for aggregate GNU extensions, especially empty structs in C, leading to special-casing that breaks ABI compatibility with C++.

Fault in `va_arg` expansion metadata for variadic functions involving empty aggregates, such as wrong gp-offset/stack advancement or wrong rounding/alignment when an empty record appears in the unnamed list.
Inconsistent handling of zero-size or empty RECORD_TYPE nodes between middle-end call construction and backend function-argument cumulative state updates, causing subsequent arguments to be shifted.

Special-case optimization or canonicalization that drops zero-sized arguments during call generation even when the ABI requires them to affect argument position for interoperability with C++ empty class objects.
evidence: The bug report explicitly states that an empty struct value is passed differently in C and C++.
The observed symptom is garbage in the sixth argument, which is classic evidence that `va_list` traversal became offset from the true argument layout after an earlier argument.
Adding any member to the empty struct makes the problem disappear, showing the failure is tied specifically to empty-aggregate handling rather than general variadic logic.
The reproducer uses a variadic function, where correctness depends completely on exact caller/callee ABI agreement for unnamed arguments.
The failure affects arguments after the empty struct rather than the empty struct itself, indicating slot consumption or alignment disagreement, not merely wrong value materialization.
The behavior summary points directly to front-end and ABI-lowering inconsistency for empty aggregate by-value arguments rather than libc implementation issues.

On x86-64 SysV, later variadic arguments are fetched according to tracked register/stack offsets, so a single misclassified aggregate readily corrupts all following `va_arg` reads, matching the report.

A mismatch for empty aggregate classification in variadic calls would most naturally live here.

Core call expansion file that decides how arguments are materialized and passed at the caller side. The bug symptom strongly suggests caller/callee disagreement over whether an empty struct consumes an argument slot, and `expand_call`-related logic is a prime place for such zero-sized argument mishandling.

Directly related to `stdarg`/`va_arg` handling on targets that track register saves and offsets. If empty aggregate arguments cause wrong gp/stack advancement metadata for variadic access, this file is a likely place for the callee-side corruption to emerge.

Very plausible root cause because the C vs C++ difference hinges on how empty records get size/alignment assigned. If GNU C empty structs are left effectively zero-sized while C++ empty classes get size 1, downstream ABI lowering would diverge exactly as reported.

The C front end constructs record types here, including GNU C extension structs. Since the bug specifically says empty struct values are passed differently in C and C++, the C-side type construction for empty records is a strong suspect.

C++ front-end class layout logic is relevant because C++ empty classes are valid object types with nonzero size. If interoperability breaks, comparing this file’s empty-class layout behavior against the C front end is highly relevant.

Handles function-level RTL generation and argument alignment helpers like `pad_to_arg_alignment`. If zero-sized aggregate arguments are being dropped or aligned inconsistently during lowering, this infrastructure could contribute to the ABI shift.

Contains C front-end argument conversion logic such as `convert_arguments`. If GNU C variadic lowering special-cases empty structs or lets zero-sized aggregate semantics leak into unnamed argument handling, this file could be involved.

Middle-end expression expansion can affect how aggregate values are represented before call lowering. A bug involving empty BLKmode/zero-sized objects being optimized away before variadic call emission could pass through here.

Less direct, but target hook defaults sometimes mediate ABI behavior when backends do not override all cases. If empty aggregate argument classification falls through generic hooks inconsistently between caller and `va_arg` logic, this file is worth checking.

Generate insns to zero all st registers together. Return true when zeroing instructions are generated. Assume the number of st registers that are zeroed is num_of_st, we will emit the following sequence to zero them together: fldz; \ fldz; \ ... fldz; \ fstp %%st(0); \ fstp %%st(0); \ ... fstp %%st(0); i.e., num_of_st fldz followed by num_of_st fstp to clear the stack mark stack slots empty. How to compute the num_of_st: There is no direct mapping from stack registers to hard register numbers. If one stack register needs to be cleared, we don't know where in the stack the value remains. So, if any stack register needs to be cleared, the whole stack should be cleared. However, x87 stack registers that hold the return value should be excluded. x87 returns in the top (two for complex values) register, so num_of_st should be 7/6 when x87 returns, otherwise it will be 8. return the value of num_of_st.

Each c_scope structure describes the complete contents of one scope. Four scopes are distinguished specially: the innermost or current scope, the innermost function scope, the file scope (always the second to outermost) and the outermost or external scope. Most declarations are recorded in the current scope. All normal label declarations are recorded in the innermost function scope, as are bindings of undeclared identifiers to error_mark_node. gcc/c/c-decl.cc.signature: static tree get_parm_array_spec (const struct c_parm *parm, tree attrs)
gcc/c/c-decl.cc.summary: Return attribute "arg spec" corresponding to an array/VLA parameter described by PARM, concatenated onto attributes ATTRS. The spec consists of one dollar symbol for each specified variable bound, one asterisk for each unspecified variable bound, followed by at most one specification of the most significant bound of an ordinary array parameter. For ordinary arrays the specification is either the constant bound itself, or the space character for an array with an unspecified bound (the [] form). Finally, a chain of specified variable bounds is appended to the spec, starting with the most significant bound. For example, the PARM T a[2][m][3][n] will produce __attribute__((arg spec ("[$$2]", m, n)). For T a typedef for an array with variable bounds, the bounds are included in the specification in the expected order. No "arg spec" is created for parameters of pointer types, making a distinction between T(*)[N] (or, equivalently, T[][N]) and the T[M][N] form, all of which have the same type and are represented the same, but only the last of which gets an "arg spec" describing the most significant bound M.

We might also be in the middle of an expression with side effects on the pointed-to type size "arguments" prior to the pointer declaration point and the fake TYPE_DECL in the enclosing context would force the size evaluation prior to the side effects. Store PARM_DECLs in PARMS into scope temporarily. Used for c_finish_omp_declare_simd for function prototypes. No diagnostics should be done.
Undo what temp_store_parm_decls did.

Finish up a function declaration and compile that function all the way to assembler language output. Then free the storage for the function definition. This is called after parsing the body of the function definition.

Check the declarations given in a for-loop for satisfying the C99 constraints. If exactly one such decl is found, return it. LOC is the location of the opening parenthesis of the for loop. The last parameter allows you to control the "for loop initial declarations are only allowed in C99 mode". Normally, you should pass flag_isoc99 as that parameter. But in some cases (Objective-C foreach loop, for example) we want to run the checks in this function even if not in C99 mode, so we allow the caller to turn off the error about not being in C99 mode.
Save and reinitialize the variables used during compilation of a C function.
Restore the variables used during compilation of a C function.
Returns the stmt_tree (if any) to which statements are currently being added. If there is no active statement-tree, NULL is returned.
Return the global value of T as a symbol.
Return the global value of tag T as a symbol.

In C, the only C-linkage public declaration is at file scope.

Return a declarator for the identifier IDENT (which may be NULL_TREE for an abstract declarator).

Return a pointer to a structure for an empty list of declaration specifiers.

Combine "long", "short", "signed", "unsigned" and "_Complex" type specifiers with any other type specifier to determine the resulting type. This is where ISO C checks on complex types are made, since "_Complex long" is a prefix of the valid ISO C type "_Complex long double". Also apply postfix standard attributes to modify the type.
Perform final processing on one file scope's declarations (or the external scope's declarations), GLOBALS.
Collect all references relevant to SOURCE_FILE.
Collect source file references at global level.
Free attribute access data that are not needed by the middle end.
Perform any final parser cleanups and generate initial debugging information.
Register reserved keyword WORD as qualifier for address space AS.

gcc/c/c-decl.cc.signature: tree c_omp_reduction_id (enum tree_code reduction_code, tree reduction_id)
gcc/c/c-decl.cc.summary: Return identifier to look up for omp declare reduction.
Lookup REDUCTION_ID in the current scope, or create an artificial VAR_DECL, bind it into the current scope and return it.
Lookup REDUCTION_ID in the first scope where it has entry for TYPE.
Helper function called via walk_tree, to diagnose invalid #pragma omp declare reduction combiners or initializers.

Searches through last statements in cur_stmt_list, stops when seeing BEFORE_LABELs, or statement other than LABEL_EXPR or CASE_LABEL_EXPR. Undoes what get_loop_names did when it returned NUM_NAMES.

gcc/c/c-decl.cc.summary: Finish processing of break or continue identifier operand. NAME is the identifier operand of break or continue and IS_BREAK is true iff it is break stmt. Returns the operand to use for BREAK_STMT or CONTINUE_STMT, either NULL_TREE or canonical loop/switch name LABEL_DECL.

gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Set CURRENT_ACCESS_SPECIFIER based on the protection of DECL.
Return a COND_EXPR that executes TRUE_STMT if this execution of the 'structor is in charge of 'structing virtual bases, or FALSE_STMT otherwise.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: tree build_base_path (enum tree_code code, tree expr, tree binfo, int nonnull, tsubst_flags_t complain)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Convert to or from a base subobject. EXPR is an expression of type `A' or `A*', an expression of type `B' or `B*' is returned. To convert A to a base B, CODE is PLUS_EXPR and BINFO is the binfo for the B base instance within A. To convert base A to derived B, CODE is MINUS_EXPR and BINFO is the binfo for the A instance within B. In this latter case, A must not be a morally virtual base of B. NONNULL is true if EXPR is known to be non-NULL (this is only needed when EXPR is of pointer type). CV qualifiers are preserved from EXPR.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: static tree build_simple_base_path (tree expr, tree binfo)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Subroutine of build_base_path; EXPR and BINFO are as in that function. Perform a derived-to-base conversion by recursively building up a sequence of COMPONENT_REFs to the appropriate base fields.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: tree convert_to_base (tree object, tree type, bool check_access, bool nonnull, tsubst_flags_t complain)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Convert OBJECT to the base TYPE. OBJECT is an expression whose type is a class type or a pointer to a class type. In the former case, TYPE is also a class type; in the latter it is another pointer type. If CHECK_ACCESS is true, an error message is emitted if TYPE is inaccessible. If OBJECT has pointer type, the value is assumed to be non-NULL.

EXPR is an expression with unqualified class type. BASE is a base binfo of that class type. Returns EXPR, converted to the BASE type. This function assumes that EXPR is the most derived class; therefore virtual bases can be found at their static offsets.

True IFF EXPR is a reference to an empty base class "subobject", as built in convert_to_base_statically. We look for the result of the fold_convert call, a NOP_EXPR from one pointer type to another, where the target is an empty base of the original type.

Given an object INSTANCE, return an expression which yields the vtable element corresponding to INDEX. There are many special cases for INSTANCE which we take care of here, mainly to avoid creating extra tree nodes when we don't have to.
Given a stable object pointer INSTANCE_PTR, return an expression which yields a function pointer corresponding to vtable element INDEX.
Return the name of the virtual function table (as an IDENTIFIER_NODE) for the given TYPE.

DECL is an entity associated with TYPE, like a virtual table or an implicitly generated constructor. Determine whether or not DECL should have external or internal linkage at the object file level. This routine does not deal with COMDAT linkage and other similar complexities; it simply sets TREE_PUBLIC if it possible for entities in other translation units to contain copies of DECL, in the abstract.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: static tree build_vtable (tree class_type, tree name, tree vtable_type)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Create a VAR_DECL for a primary or secondary vtable for CLASS_TYPE. (For a secondary vtable for B-in-D, CLASS_TYPE should be D, not B.) Use NAME for the name of the vtable, and VTABLE_TYPE for its type.

Get the VAR_DECL of the vtable for TYPE. TYPE need not be polymorphic, or even complete. If this does not exist, create it. If COMPLETE is nonzero, then complete the definition of it -- that will render it impossible to actually build the vtable, but is useful to get at those which are known to exist in the runtime.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: static int build_primary_vtable (tree binfo, tree type)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Build the primary virtual function table for TYPE. If BINFO is non-NULL, build the vtable starting with the initial approximation that it is the same as the one which is the head of the association list. Returns a nonzero value if a new vtable is actually created.

Give BINFO a new virtual function table which is initialized with a skeleton-copy of its original initialization. The only entry that changes is the `delta' entry, so we can really share a lot of structure. FOR_TYPE is the most derived type which caused this table to be needed. Returns nonzero if we haven't met BINFO before. The order in which vtables are built (by calling this function) for an object must remain the same, otherwise a binary incompatibility can result.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: static int make_new_vtable (tree t, tree binfo)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Create a new vtable for BINFO which is the hierarchy dominated by T. Return nonzero if we actually created a new vtable.

gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Make *VIRTUALS, an entry on the BINFO_VIRTUALS list for BINFO (which is in the hierarchy dominated by T) list FNDECL as its BV_FN. DELTA is the required constant adjustment from the `this' pointer where the vtable entry appears to the `this' required when the function is actually called.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: bool object_parms_correspond (tree fn, tree method, tree context)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: True if FN and METHOD have corresponding object parms per [basic.scope.scope], or if one of them is a static member function (which are considered to have an object parm that corresponds to any other). CONTEXT is the class that an implicit object member function is considered to be a member of for the purpose of this comparison, per [over.match.funcs].

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: bool add_method (tree type, tree method, bool via_using)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Add method METHOD to class TYPE. If VIA_USING indicates whether METHOD is being injected via a using_decl. Returns true if the method could be added to the method vec.

Return the access node for DECL's access in its enclosing class.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: static void handle_using_decl (tree using_decl, tree t)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Process the USING_DECL, which is a member of T.

walk_tree callback for check_abi_tags: if the type at *TP involves any types with ABI tags, add the corresponding identifiers to the VEC in DATA and set IDENTIFIER_MARKED.
walk_tree callback for mark_abi_tags: if *TP is a class, set IDENTIFIER_MARKED on its ABI tags.

gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Check that T has all the ABI tags that subobject SUBOB has, or warn if not. If T is a (variable or function) declaration, also return any missing tags, and add them to T if JUST_CHECKING is false.
Check that DECL has all the ABI tags that are used in parts of its type that are not reflected in its mangled name.

Return true, iff class T has a non-virtual destructor that is accessible from outside the class heirarchy (i.e. is public, or there's a suitable friend.

Determine all the primary bases within T. Sets BINFO_PRIMARY_BASE_P for those that are primaries. Sets BINFO_LOST_PRIMARY_P for those that have had a nearly-empty virtual primary base stolen by some other base in the hierarchy. Determines CLASSTYPE_PRIMARY_BASE for T.
Update the variant types of T.

Issue warnings about T having private constructors, but no friends, and so forth. HAS_NONPRIVATE_METHOD is nonzero if T has any non-private methods or static members. HAS_NONPRIVATE_STATIC_FN is nonzero if T has any non-private static member functions.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: static void layout_vtable_decl (tree binfo, int n)

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: static void get_basefndecls (tree name, tree t, vec<tree> *base_fndecls)

Warn about hidden virtual functions that are not overridden in t. We know that constructors and destructors don't apply.
Recursive helper for finish_struct_anon.
Fix up any anonymous union/struct members of T.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: void maybe_add_class_template_decl_list (tree type, tree t, int friend_p)

This function is called from declare_virt_assop_and_dtor via dfs_walk_all. DATA is a type that direcly or indirectly inherits the base represented by BINFO. If BINFO contains a virtual assignment [copy assignment or move assigment] operator or a virtual constructor, declare that function in DATA if it hasn't been already declared.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: static void one_inheriting_sig (tree t, tree ctor, tree *parms, int nparms)

Build the VTT (virtual table table) for T. A class requires a VTT if it has virtual bases. This holds 1 - primary virtual pointer for complete object T 2 - secondary VTTs for each direct non-virtual base of T which requires a VTT 3 - secondary virtual pointers for each direct or indirect base of T which has virtual bases or is reachable via a virtual path from T. 4 - secondary VTTs for each direct or indirect virtual base of T. Secondary VTTs look like complete object VTTs without part 4.

When building a secondary VTT, BINFO_VTABLE is set to a TREE_LIST with PURPOSE the RTTI_BINFO, VALUE the real vtable pointer for this binfo, and CHAIN the vtable pointer for this binfo after construction is complete. VALUE can also be another BINFO, in which case we recurse.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: static void build_vtt_inits (tree binfo, tree t, vec<constructor_elt, va_gc> **inits, tree *index)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Recursively build the VTT-initializer for BINFO (which is in the hierarchy dominated by T). INITS points to the end of the initializer list to date. INDEX is the VTT index where the next element will be replaced. Iff BINFO is the binfo for T, this is the top level VTT (i.e. not a subvtt for some base of T). When that is so, we emit the sub-VTTs for virtual bases of T. When it is not so, we build the constructor vtables for the BINFO-in-T variant.
Called from build_vtt_inits via dfs_walk. BINFO is the binfo for the base in most derived. DATA is a SECONDARY_VPTR_VTT_INIT_DATA structure.

gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Add the vtbl initializers for BINFO (and its bases other than non-virtual primaries) to the list of INITS. BINFO is in the hierarchy dominated by T. RTTI_BINFO is the binfo within T of the constructor the vtbl inits should be accumulated for. (If this is the complete object vtbl then RTTI_BINFO will be TYPE_BINFO (T).) ORIG_BINFO is the binfo for this object within BINFO_TYPE (RTTI_BINFO). BINFO is the active base equivalent of ORIG_BINFO in the inheritance graph of T. Both BINFO and ORIG_BINFO will have the same BINFO_TYPE, but are not necessarily the same in terms of layout.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: static void dfs_accumulate_vtbl_inits (tree binfo, tree orig_binfo, tree rtti_binfo, tree orig_vtbl, tree t, vec<constructor_elt, va_gc> **l)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Called from accumulate_vtbl_inits. Adds the initializers for the BINFO vtable to L.

gcc/cp/class.cc.signature: static void build_vtbl_initializer (tree binfo, tree orig_binfo, tree t, tree rtti_binfo, int* non_fn_entries_p, vec<constructor_elt, va_gc> **inits)
gcc/cp/class.cc.summary: Construct the initializer for BINFO's virtual function table. BINFO is part of the hierarchy dominated by T. If we're building a construction vtable, the ORIG_BINFO is the binfo we should use to find the actual function pointers to put in the vtable - but they can be overridden on the path to most-derived in the graph that ORIG_BINFO belongs. Otherwise, ORIG_BINFO should be the same as BINFO. The RTTI_BINFO is the BINFO that should be indicated by the RTTI information in the vtable; it will be a base class of T, rather than T itself, if we are building a construction vtable. The value returned is a TREE_LIST suitable for wrapping in a CONSTRUCTOR to use as the DECL_INITIAL for a vtable. If NON_FN_ENTRIES_P is not NULL, *NON_FN_ENTRIES_P is set to the number of non-function entries in the vtable. It might seem that this function should never be called with a BINFO for which BINFO_PRIMARY_P holds, the vtable for such a base is always subsumed by a derived class vtable. However, when we are building construction vtables, we do build vtables for primary bases; we need these while the primary base is being constructed.

gcc/function.cc.summary: This mini-pass fixes fall-out from SSA in asm statements that have in-out constraints. Say you start with orig = inout; asm ("": "+mr" (inout)); use (orig); which is transformed very early to use explicit output and match operands: orig = inout; asm ("": "=mr" (inout) : "0" (inout)); use (orig); Or, after SSA and copyprop, asm ("": "=mr" (inout_2) : "0" (inout_1)); use (inout_1); Clearly inout_2 and inout_1 can't be coalesced easily anymore, as they represent two separate values, so they will get different pseudo registers during expansion. Then, since the two operands need to match per the constraints, but use different pseudo registers, reload can only register a reload for these operands. But reloads can only be satisfied by hardregs, not by memory, so we need a register for this reload, just because we are presented with non-matching operands. So, even though we allow memory for this operand, no memory can be used for it, just because the two operands don't match. This can cause reload failures on register-starved targets. So it's a symptom of reload not being able to use memory for reloads or, alternatively it's also a symptom of both operands not coming into reload as matchin

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Build an array type. This sets typeless storage as required by C2Y and C_TYPE_VARIABLY_MODIFIED and C_TYPE_VARIABLE_SIZE based on the element type and domain.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree c_build_array_type_unspecified (tree type)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Build an array type of unspecified size.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree c_build_type_attribute_qual_variant (tree type, tree attrs, int quals)
tree c_build_type_attribute_variant (tree type, tree attrs)
tree c_reconstruct_complex_type (tree type, tree bottom)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Reconstruct a complex derived type. This is used to re-construct types with the vector attribute. It is called via a langhook.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree c_build_functype_attribute_variant (tree ntype, tree otype, tree attrs)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: If NTYPE is a type of a non-variadic function with a prototype and OTYPE is a type of a function without a prototype and ATTRS contains attribute format, diagnosess and removes it from ATTRS. Returns the result of build_type_attribute_variant of NTYPE and the (possibly) modified ATTRS.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static const_tree c_type_original (const_tree t)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Given a type which could be a typedef name, make sure to return the original type. See set_underlying_type.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree c_type_tag (const_tree t)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return the tag for a tagged type.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree composite_type_internal (tree t1, tree t2, struct composite_cache* cache)
tree composite_type (tree t1, tree t2)
static tree common_pointer_type (tree t1, tree t2)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return the type of a conditional expression between pointers to possibly differently qualified versions of compatible types. We assume that comp_target_types has already been done and returned true; if that isn't so, this may crash.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree c_common_type (tree t1, tree t2)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return the common type for two arithmetic types under the usual arithmetic conversions. The default conversions have already been applied, and enumerated types converted to their compatible integer types. The resulting type is unqualified and has no attributes. This is the type for the result of most arithmetic operations if the operands have the given two types.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree common_type (tree t1, tree t2)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Wrapper around c_common_type that is used by c-common.cc and other front end optimizations that remove promotions. ENUMERAL_TYPEs are allowed here and are converted to their compatible integer types. BOOLEAN_TYPEs are allowed here and return either boolean_type_node or preferably a non-Boolean type as the common type.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static bool comptypes_verify (tree type1, tree type2)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Helper function for comptypes. For two compatible types, return 1 if they pass consistency checks. In particular we test that TYPE_CANONICAL is set correctly, i.e. the two types can alias.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: bool compatible_types_for_indirection_note_p (tree type1, tree type2)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: C implementation of compatible_types_for_indirection_note_p.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: int comptypes (tree type1, tree type2)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return 1 if TYPE1 and TYPE2 are compatible types for assignment or various other operations. Return 2 if they are compatible but a warning may be needed if you use them together.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: bool comptypes_same_p (tree type1, tree type2)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Like comptypes, but it returns non-zero only for identical types.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: int comptypes_check_enum_int (tree type1, tree type2, bool *enum_and_int_p)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Like comptypes, but if it returns non-zero because enum and int are compatible, it sets *ENUM_AND_INT_P to true.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: int comptypes_check_different_types (tree type1, tree type2, bool *different_types_p)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Like comptypes, but if it returns nonzero for different types, it sets *DIFFERENT_TYPES_P to true.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: bool comptypes_equiv_p (tree type1, tree type2)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Like comptypes, but if it returns true for struct and union types considered equivalent for aliasing purposes, i.e. for setting TYPE_CANONICAL after completing a struct or union. This function must return false only for types which are not compatible according to C language semantics (cf. comptypes), otherwise the middle-end would make incorrect aliasing decisions. It may return true for some similar types that are not compatible according to those stricter rules. In particular, we ignore size expression in arrays so that the following structs are in the same equivalence class: struct foo { char (*buf)[]; }; struct foo { char (*buf)[3]; }; struct foo { char (*buf)[4]; }; We also treat unions / structs with members which are pointers to structures or unions with the same tag as equivalent (if they are not incompatible for other reasons). Although incomplete structure or union types are not compatible to any other type, they may become compatible to different types when completed. To avoid having to update TYPE_CANONICAL at this point, we only consider the tag when forming the equivalence classes. For example, the following types with tag 'foo' are all considered equivalent: struct b

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static bool comptypes_internal (const_tree type1, const_tree type2, struct comptypes_data *data)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return true if TYPE1 and TYPE2 are compatible types for assignment or various other operations. If they are compatible but a warning may be needed if you use them together, 'warning_needed' in DATA is set. If one type is an enum and the other a compatible integer type, then this sets 'enum_and_int_p' in DATA to true (it is never set to false). If the types are compatible but different enough not to be permitted in C11 typedef redeclarations, then this sets 'different_types_p' in DATA to true; it is never set to false, but may or may not be set if the types are incompatible. This differs from comptypes, in that we don't free the seen types.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static bool comp_target_types (location_t location, tree ttl, tree ttr)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return true if TTL and TTR are pointers to types that are equivalent, ignoring their qualifiers, except for named address spaces. If the pointers point to different named addresses, then we must determine if one address space is a subset of the other.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static bool tagged_types_tu_compatible_p (const_tree t1, const_tree t2, struct comptypes_data *data)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return true if two 'struct', 'union', or 'enum' types T1 and T2 are compatible. The two types are not the same (which has been checked earlier in comptypes_internal).

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static bool function_types_compatible_p (const_tree f1, const_tree f2, struct comptypes_data *data)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return true if two function types F1 and F2 are compatible. If either type specifies no argument types, the other must specify a fixed number of self-promoting arg types. Otherwise, if one type specifies only the number of arguments, the other must specify that number of self-promoting arg types. Otherwise, the argument types must match.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static bool type_lists_compatible_p (const_tree args1, const_tree args2, struct comptypes_data *data)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Check two lists of types for compatibility, returning false for incompatible, true for compatible.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree c_size_in_bytes (const_tree type)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Compute the size to increment a pointer by. When a function type or void type or incomplete type is passed, size_one_node is returned. This function does not emit any diagnostics; the caller is responsible for that.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree decl_constant_value_1 (tree decl, bool in_init)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return either DECL or its known constant value (if it has one).

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree decl_constant_value (tree decl)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return either DECL or its known constant value (if it has one). Like the above, but always return decl outside of functions.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree array_to_pointer_conversion (location_t loc, tree exp)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Convert the array expression EXP to a pointer.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree function_to_pointer_conversion (location_t loc, tree exp)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Convert the function expression EXP to a pointer.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: void mark_exp_read (tree exp)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Mark EXP as read, not just set, for set but not used -Wunused warning purposes.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: struct c_expr default_function_array_conversion (location_t loc, struct c_expr exp)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Perform the default conversion of arrays and functions to pointers. Return the result of converting EXP. For any other expression, just return EXP. LOC is the location of the expression.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: struct c_expr default_function_array_read_conversion (location_t loc, struct c_expr exp)
static bool really_atomic_lvalue (tree expr)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return whether EXPR should be treated as an atomic lvalue for the purposes of load and store handling.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree maybe_get_constexpr_init (tree expr)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: If EXPR is a named constant (C23) derived from a constexpr variable - that is, a reference to such a variable, or a member extracted by a sequence of structure and union (but not array) member accesses (where union member accesses must access the same member as initialized) - then return the corresponding initializer; otherwise, return NULL_TREE.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: struct c_expr convert_lvalue_to_rvalue (location_t loc, struct c_expr exp, bool convert_p, bool read_p, bool for_init)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Convert expression EXP (location LOC) from lvalue to rvalue, including converting functions and arrays to pointers if CONVERT_P. If READ_P, also mark the expression as having been read. If FOR_INIT, constexpr expressions of structure and union type should be replaced by the corresponding CONSTRUCTOR; otherwise, only constexpr scalars (including elements of structures and unions) are replaced by their initializers.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree perform_integral_promotions (tree exp)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: EXP is an expression of integer type. Apply the integer promotions to it and return the promoted value.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree default_conversion (tree exp)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Perform default promotions for C data used in expressions. Enumeral types or short or char are converted to int. In addition, manifest constants symbols are replaced by their values.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree lookup_field (const_tree type, tree component)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Look up COMPONENT in a structure or union TYPE. If the component name is not found, returns NULL_TREE. Otherwise, the return value is a TREE_LIST, with each TREE_VALUE a FIELD_DECL stepping down the chain to the component, which is in the last TREE_VALUE of the list. Normally the list is of length one, but if the component is embedded within (nested) anonymous structures or unions, the list steps down the chain to the component.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static void lookup_field_fuzzy_find_candidates (tree type, tree component, vec<tree> *candidates)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Recursively append candidate IDENTIFIER_NODEs to CANDIDATES.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree lookup_field_fuzzy (tree type, tree component)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Like "lookup_field", but find the closest matching IDENTIFIER_NODE, rather than returning a TREE_LIST for an exact match.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static bool should_suggest_deref_p (tree datum_type)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Support function for build_component_ref's error-handling. Given DATUM_TYPE, and "DATUM.COMPONENT", where DATUM is *not* a struct or union, should we suggest "DATUM->COMPONENT" as a hint?

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree build_counted_by_ref (tree datum, tree subdatum, tree *counted_by_type)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: For a SUBDATUM field of a structure or union DATUM, generate a REF to the object that represents its counted_by per the attribute counted_by attached to this field if it's a flexible array member field, otherwise return NULL_TREE. Set COUNTED_BY_TYPE to the TYPE of the counted_by field. For example, if: struct P { int k; int x[] __attribute__ ((counted_by (k))); } *p; for: p->x the ref to the object that represents its element count will be: &(p->k)

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree build_access_with_size_for_counted_by (location_t loc, tree ref, tree counted_by_ref, tree counted_by_type)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Given a COMPONENT_REF REF with the location LOC, the corresponding COUNTED_BY_REF, and the COUNTED_BY_TYPE, generate an INDIRECT_REF to a call to the internal function .ACCESS_WITH_SIZE. REF to: (*.ACCESS_WITH_SIZE (REF, COUNTED_BY_REF, 1, (TYPE_OF_SIZE)0, -1, (TYPE_OF_ARRAY *)0)) NOTE: The return type of this function is the POINTER type pointing to the original flexible array type. Then the type of the INDIRECT_REF is the original flexible array type. The type of the first argument of this function is a POINTER type to the original flexible array type. The 4th argument of the call is a constant 0 with the TYPE of the object pointed by COUNTED_BY_REF. The 6th argument of the call is a constant 0 with the pointer TYPE to the original flexible array type.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree handle_counted_by_for_component_ref (location_t loc, tree ref)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: For the COMPONENT_REF ref, check whether it has a counted_by attribute, if so, wrap this COMPONENT_REF with the corresponding CALL to the function .ACCESS_WITH_SIZE. Otherwise, return the ref itself.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree build_component_ref (location_t loc, tree datum, tree component, location_t component_loc, location_t arrow_loc, bool handle_counted_by)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Make an expression to refer to the COMPONENT field of structure or union value DATUM. COMPONENT is an IDENTIFIER_NODE. LOC is the location of the COMPONENT_REF. COMPONENT_LOC is the location of COMPONENT. ARROW_LOC is the location of the first -> operand if it is from -> operator. If HANDLE_COUNTED_BY is true, check the counted_by attribute and generate a call to .ACCESS_WITH_SIZE. Otherwise, ignore the attribute.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree build_indirect_ref (location_t loc, tree ptr, ref_operator errstring)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Given an expression PTR for a pointer, return an expression for the value pointed to. ERRORSTRING is the name of the operator to appear in error messages. LOC is the location to use for the generated tree.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree build_array_ref (location_t loc, tree array, tree index)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: This handles expressions of the form "a[i]", which denotes an array reference. This is logically equivalent in C to *(a+i), but we may do it differently. If A is a variable or a member, we generate a primitive ARRAY_REF. This avoids forcing the array out of registers, and can work on arrays that are not lvalues (for example, members of structures returned by functions). For vector types, allow vector[i] but not i[vector], and create (((type*)&vectortype) + i) for the expression. LOC is the location to use for the returned expression.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree build_omp_array_section (location_t loc, tree array, tree index, tree length)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Build an OpenMP array section reference, creating an exact type for the resulting expression based on the element type and bounds if possible. If we have variable bounds, create an incomplete array type for the result instead.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree build_external_ref (location_t loc, tree id, bool fun, tree *type)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Build an external reference to identifier ID. FUN indicates whether this will be used for a function call. LOC is the source location of the identifier. This sets *TYPE to the type of the identifier, which is not the same as the type of the returned value for CONST_DECLs defined as enum constants. If the type of the identifier is not available, *TYPE is set to NULL.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static void record_maybe_used_decl (tree decl)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Record that DECL, an undefined static function reference seen inside sizeof or typeof, might be used if the operand of sizeof is a VLA type or the operand of typeof is a variably modified type.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: void pop_maybe_used (bool used)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Pop the stack of decls possibly used inside sizeof or typeof. If USED is false, just discard them. If it is true, mark them used (if no longer inside sizeof or typeof) or move them to the next level up (if still inside sizeof or typeof).

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: struct c_expr c_expr_sizeof_expr (location_t loc, struct c_expr expr)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return the result of sizeof applied to EXPR.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: struct c_expr c_expr_sizeof_type (location_t loc, struct c_type_name *t)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return the result of sizeof applied to T, a structure for the type name passed to sizeof (rather than the type itself). LOC is the location of the original expression.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree build_function_call (location_t loc, tree function, tree params)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Build a function call to function FUNCTION with parameters PARAMS. The function call is at LOC. PARAMS is a list--a chain of TREE_LIST nodes--in which the TREE_VALUE of each node is a parameter-expression. FUNCTION's data type may be a function type or a pointer-to-function.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static void inform_declaration (tree decl, tree function_expr)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Give a note about the location of the declaration of DECL, or, failing that, a pertinent declaration for FUNCTION_EXPR.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static bool comp_parm_types (tree wanted_type, tree actual_type)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: C implementation of callback for use when checking param types.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree build_function_call_vec (location_t loc, vec<location_t> arg_loc, tree function, vec<tree, va_gc> *params, vec<tree, va_gc> *origtypes, tree orig_fundecl)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Build a function call to function FUNCTION with parameters PARAMS. If FUNCTION is the result of resolving an overloaded target built-in, ORIG_FUNDECL is the original function decl, otherwise it is null. ORIGTYPES, if not NULL, is a vector of types; each element is either NULL or the original type of the corresponding element in PARAMS. The original type may differ from TREE_TYPE of the parameter for enums. FUNCTION's data type may be a function type or pointer-to-function. This function changes the elements of PARAMS.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree c_build_function_call_vec (location_t loc, const vec<location_t> &arg_loc, tree function, vec<tree, va_gc> *params, vec<tree, va_gc> *origtypes)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Like build_function_call_vec, but call also resolve_overloaded_builtin.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree convert_argument (location_t ploc, tree function, tree fundecl, tree type, tree origtype, tree val, tree valtype, bool npc, tree rname, int parmnum, int argnum, bool excess_precision, int warnopt)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Helper for convert_arguments called to convert the VALue of argument number ARGNUM from ORIGTYPE to the corresponding parameter number PARMNUM and TYPE. PLOC is the location where the conversion is being performed. FUNCTION and FUNDECL are the same as in convert_arguments. VALTYPE is the original type of VAL before the conversion and, for EXCESS_PRECISION_EXPR, the operand of the expression. NPC is true if VAL represents the null pointer constant (VAL itself will have been folded to an integer constant). RNAME is the same as FUNCTION except in Objective C when it's the function selector. EXCESS_PRECISION is true when VAL was originally represented as EXCESS_PRECISION_EXPR. WARNOPT is the same as in convert_for_assignment.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static int convert_arguments (location_t loc, vec<location_t> arg_loc, tree fntype, vec<tree, va_gc> *values, vec<tree, va_gc> *origtypes, tree function, tree fundecl)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Convert the argument expressions in the vector VALUES to the types in the list TYPE_ARG_TYPES (FNTYPE). If the list is exhausted, or when an element has NULL as its type, perform the default conversions. ORIGTYPES is the original types of the expressions in VALUES. This holds the type of enum values which have been converted to integral types. It may be NULL. FUNCTION is a tree for the called function. It is used only for error messages, where it is formatted with %qE. This is also where warnings about wrong number of args are generated. ARG_LOC are locations of function arguments (if any). Returns the actual number of arguments processed (which may be less than the length of VALUES in some error situations), or -1 on failure.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: struct c_expr parser_build_unary_op (location_t loc, enum tree_code code, struct c_expr arg)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: This is the entry point used by the parser to build unary operators in the input. CODE, a tree_code, specifies the unary operator, and ARG is the operand. For unary plus, the C parser currently uses CONVERT_EXPR for code. LOC is the location to use for the tree generated.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: bool char_type_p (tree type)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Returns true if TYPE is a character type, *not* including wchar_t.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: struct c_expr parser_build_binary_op (location_t location, enum tree_code code, struct c_expr arg1, struct c_expr arg2)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: This is the entry point used by the parser to build binary operators in the input. CODE, a tree_code, specifies the binary operator, and ARG1 and ARG2 are the operands. In addition to constructing the expression, we check for operands that were written with other binary operators in a way that is likely to confuse the user. LOCATION is the location of the binary operator.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree pointer_diff (location_t loc, tree op0, tree op1, tree *instrument_expr)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return a tree for the difference of pointers OP0 and OP1. The resulting tree has type ptrdiff_t. If POINTER_SUBTRACT sanitization is enabled, assign to INSTRUMENT_EXPR call to libsanitizer.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree build_atomic_assign (location_t loc, tree lhs, enum tree_code modifycode, tree rhs, bool return_old_p)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Build an atomic assignment at LOC, expanding into the proper sequence to store LHS MODIFYCODE= RHS. Return a value representing the result of the operation, unless RETURN_OLD_P, in which case return the old value of LHS (this is only for postincrement and postdecrement).

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree build_unary_op (location_t location, enum tree_code code, tree xarg, bool noconvert)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Construct and perhaps optimize a tree representation for a unary operation. CODE, a tree_code, specifies the operation and XARG is the operand. For any CODE other than ADDR_EXPR, NOCONVERT suppresses the default promotions (such as from short to int). For ADDR_EXPR, the default promotions are not applied; NOCONVERT allows non-lvalues; this is only used to handle conversion of non-lvalue arrays to pointers in C99. LOCATION is the location of the operator.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: bool lvalue_p (const_tree ref)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return nonzero if REF is an lvalue valid for this language. Lvalues can be assigned, unless their type has TYPE_READONLY. Lvalues can have their address taken, unless they have C_DECL_REGISTER.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static void readonly_warning (tree arg, enum lvalue_use use)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Give a warning for storing in something that is read-only in GCC terms but not const in ISO C terms.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static int lvalue_or_else (location_t loc, const_tree ref, enum lvalue_use use)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Return nonzero if REF is an lvalue valid for this language; otherwise, print an error message and return zero. USE says how the lvalue is being used and so selects the error message. LOCATION is the location at which any error should be reported.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: bool c_mark_addressable (tree exp, bool array_ref_p)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Mark EXP saying that we need to be able to take the address of it; it should not be allocated in a register. Returns true if successful. ARRAY_REF_P is true if this is for ARRAY_REF construction - in that case we don't want to look through VIEW_CONVERT_EXPR from VECTOR_TYPE to ARRAY_TYPE, it is fine to use ARRAY_REFs for vector subscripts on vector register variables.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree ep_convert_and_check (location_t loc, tree type, tree expr, tree semantic_type)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Convert EXPR to TYPE, warning about conversion problems with constants. SEMANTIC_TYPE is the type this conversion would use without excess precision. If SEMANTIC_TYPE is NULL, this function is equivalent to convert_and_check. This function is a wrapper that handles conversions that may be different than the usual ones because of excess precision.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree type_or_builtin_type (tree expr, tree *bltin = NULL)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: If EXPR refers to a built-in declared without a prototype returns the actual type of the built-in and, if non-null, set *BLTIN to a pointer to the built-in. Otherwise return the type of EXPR and clear *BLTIN if non-null.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree build_conditional_expr (location_t colon_loc, tree ifexp, bool ifexp_bcp, tree op1, tree op1_original_type, location_t op1_loc, tree op2, tree op2_original_type, location_t op2_loc)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Build and return a conditional expression IFEXP ? OP1 : OP2. If IFEXP_BCP then the condition is a call to __builtin_constant_p, and if folded to an integer constant then the unselected half may contain arbitrary operations not normally permitted in constant expressions. Set the location of the expression to LOC.

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static void maybe_warn_nodiscard (location_t loc, tree expr)
gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: EXPR is an expression, location LOC, whose result is discarded. Warn if it is a call to a nodiscard function (or a COMPOUND_EXPR whose right-hand operand is such a call, possibly recursively).

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: tree build_compound_expr (location_t loc, tree expr1, tree expr2)

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree convert_for_assignment (location_t location, location_t expr_loc, tree type, tree rhs, tree origtype, enum impl_conv errtype, bool null_pointer_constant, tree fundecl, tree function, int parmnum, int warnopt )

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.signature: static tree digest_init (location_t init_loc, tree decl, tree type, tree init, tree origtype, bool null_pointer_constant, bool int_const_expr, bool arith_const_expr, bool strict_string, bool require_constant, bool require_constexpr)

gcc/c/c-typeck.cc.summary: Helper function for handle_omp_array_sections. Called recursively to handle multiple array-section-subscripts. C is the clause, T current expression (initially OMP_CLAUSE_DECL), which is either a TREE_LIST for array-section-subscript (TREE_PURPOSE is low-bound expression if specified, TREE_VALUE length expression if specified, TREE_CHAIN is what it has been specified after, or some decl. TYPES vector is populated with array section types, MAYBE_ZERO_LEN set to true if any of the array-section-subscript could have length of zero (explicit or implicit), FIRST_NON_ONE is the index of the first array-section-subscript which is known not to have length of one. Given say: map(a[:b][2:1][:c][:2][:d][e:f][2:5]) FIRST_NON_ONE will be 3, array-section-subscript [:b], [2:1] and [:c] all are or may have length of 1, array-section-subscript [:2] is the first one known not to have length 1. For array-section-subscript <= FIRST_NON_ONE we diagnose non-contiguous arrays if low bound isn't 0 or length isn't the array domain max + 1, for > FIRST_NON_ONE we can if MAYBE_ZERO_LEN is false. MAYBE_ZERO_LEN will be true in the above case though, as some lengths could be zero.

MIN_SIZE is the minimal size of block to move MAX_SIZE is the maximal size of block to move, if it cannot be represented in unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT, than it is mask of all ones. CTZ_SIZE is the trailing-zeros count of SIZE; even a nonconstant SIZE is known to be a multiple of 1<<CTZ_SIZE. Return the address of the new block, if memcpy is called and returns it, 0 otherwise.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: rtx emit_block_cmp_hints (rtx x, rtx y, rtx len, tree len_type, rtx target, bool equality_only, by_pieces_constfn y_cfn, void *y_cfndata, unsigned ctz_len)

LEN_TYPE is the type of the expression that was used to calculate it, and CTZ_LEN is the known trailing-zeros count of LEN, so LEN must be a multiple of 1<<CTZ_LEN even if it's not constant. Optionally, the caller can pass a constfn and associated data in Y_CFN and Y_CFN_DATA. describing that the second operand being compared is a known constant and how to obtain its data.
